name: Valencia
tagline: Wood-fired rice in L'Albufera, two Michelin stars downtown, and Spain's most photogenic market.

Ricard Camarena Restaurant.description: Valencian produce cuisine of the highest technical level, from chef Ricard Camarena. Two Michelin stars.

El Poblet.description: Rice dishes and avant-garde Mediterranean cuisine right in downtown Valencia. Two Michelin stars.

Arrocería Maribel.description: A rice restaurant in El Palmar, the heart of L'Albufera, the historic birthplace of Valencian paella. Bib Gourmand.

Mercado Central.description: One of Europe's largest covered markets, with stalls for horchata, ham, and fresh seafood.

RiFF.description: Creative, slightly anarchic Mediterranean cuisine from chef Bernd Knöller. Valencia's oldest Michelin star, since 2009.

Fierro.description: Restaurant from chefs Germán Carrizo and Carito Lourenço, with touches of the chef's native Argentine cuisine. One Michelin star and a Repsol Sun, in an intimate space seating just 18 near Ruzafa market.

Lienzo.description: Seasonal Mediterranean cuisine from Murcia-born chef María José Martínez, with nods to the Valencian market gardens and honey from her own beehive. One Michelin star since 2021.

La Salita.description: Restaurant from Begoña Rodrigo, winner of Top Chef Spain, set in an 1866 building in Ruzafa. Cooking centered on vegetables and seafood. One Michelin star and two Repsol Suns.

Kaido Sushi Bar.description: A ten-seat edomae omakase counter run by chef Yoshikazu Yanome. The only Michelin-starred Japanese restaurant in the Valencian Community.

Fraula.description: Project from chef Roseta Félix and her team steps from the Mercado de Colón, with seasonal menus built around garden and seafood produce. One Michelin star.

Habitual.description: Ricard Camarena's second project, set in the courtyard of the IVAM museum. Market cooking in a more casual format than his flagship restaurant, holding a Repsol Sun.

Apicius.description: A fine-dining restaurant in Valencia's Eixample district serving product-driven Mediterranean cuisine, awarded a Repsol Sun.

Entrevins.description: Wine shop and restaurant in the historic center, with one of the city's most complete wine lists and market-driven cooking. Repsol Sun.

2 Estaciones.description: Market-cuisine restaurant near the Estación del Norte train station, holding a Repsol Sun and a neighborhood feel.

Canalla Bistro.description: Ricard Camarena's casual bistro in the Eixample district, with Asian- and Latin American-influenced sharing plates. One Repsol Sun.

Central Bar.description: Ricard Camarena's almuerzo counter inside the Mercado Central, famous for its pork loin sandwich and market stews. Open mornings only.

Saiti.description: Restaurant from chef Vicente Patiño in Ruzafa, holding a Michelin Bib Gourmand and two Repsol Suns.

Tandem.description: A casual dining spot near the Ayuntamiento specializing in rice dishes and traditional Valencian home cooking.

Askua.description: A benchmark grill house in Valencia since 1994, specializing in charcoal-grilled meats and seasonal produce. One Repsol Sun.

Vuelve Carolina.description: Chef Quique Dacosta's casual project inside the Mercado de Colón, holding a Michelin Bib Gourmand and a Repsol Sun.

Casa Montaña.description: A century-and-a-half-old bodega (1836) in the seafaring Cabanyal district, with a modernist façade, an extensive wine list, and Valencian tapas.

La Pepica.description: A rice restaurant facing Malvarrosa beach since 1898, once frequented by Ernest Hemingway. Traditional paellas with sea views.

Casa Carmela.description: A family-run rice restaurant since 1922 by Malvarrosa beach, famous for cooking paella over orange-wood fire.

Nou Racó.description: A rice restaurant on the shore of the Albufera lake in El Palmar, open since 1960, specializing in all i pebre and traditional rice dishes.

La Pilareta.description: A tavern serving clóchinas (Valencian mussels) since 1917 in the Barrio del Carmen, known locally as 'the house of the cloxines.'

Horchatería Santa Catalina.description: A century-old horchatería and chocolate house on Plaza de Santa Catalina, decorated with Manises tiles and now run by the fourth generation of the Gargallo family.

Horchatería El Siglo.description: A historic horchatería serving horchata since 1836 across from Santa Catalina, one of the oldest in Valencia.

Horchatería Daniel.description: A landmark horchatería in Alboraya since the mid-20th century, visited by Salvador Dalí and Rafael Alberti. Artisanal horchata and fartons.

Alejandro del Toro.description: Chef Alejandro del Toro's namesake restaurant, opened in 2001 and awarded a Michelin star in 2003. Updated, product-driven Valencian cuisine.

Bodega Anyora.description: A charming bodega in the Cabanyal district serving Valencian cuisine built on fresh produce and seafaring history.

Nori Izakaya.description: An izakaya in the Abastos area where fresh market fish takes center stage.

El Observatorio.description: A nikkei restaurant in the Patraix neighborhood, with ceviche and causa limeña among its specialties.

Bodega La Aldeana 1927.description: A restored century-old bodega in the Cabanyal district, serving 100% Valencian cuisine and local wines.

La Cooperativa del Mar.description: A former Ruzafa fishmonger turned bar specializing in Portuguese-inspired tinned seafood.

Rausell.description: One of Valencia's most characterful bars, running since the 1940s and famous for its patatas bravas.

Hikari Yakitori Bar.description: A yakitori counter in Ruzafa, grilling skewers built on the day's market produce.

Àtic. Palau Alameda.description: A Mediterranean restaurant focused on sustainable, zero-kilometer cooking, set inside the renovated Palau Alameda.

Trattoria Napoletana Da Carlo.description: A Neapolitan trattoria with more than 25 years of history in Valencia, known for traditional pizza made the old-fashioned way.

Tavella.description: A restaurant set in a 200-year-old farmhouse in Valencia's market-garden belt, serving wood-fired rice dishes and grilled meats.

Mercado de Colón.description: A 1914 modernist market building designed by architect Francisco Mora, now a gastronomic hub of cafés, horchaterías, and restaurants.
